messages.subject: inla posterior sampler evaluation
parts:
I am looking at using the posterior sampler as an alternative to getting fitted values from the model, because adding the prediction set with the output variable set to NA can sometimes stress INLA for larger prediction sets.  Is there a simple way, using inla.posterior.sample.eval, to just generate fitted values similar to those that would show up through the “typical” prediction system in $summary.fitted.values?

 

As I see it, this would involve (1) calling every predictor in the model (as opposed to just some) and (2) using rnorm as appropriate when new levels of a latent group are encountered (e.g., new levels of a random effect, akin to allow.new.levels of lme4).  Is there a straightforward way to do this without specifying each individual predictor in the model?

 

Many thanks,

Jonathan

 

Sent from Mail for Windows 10

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla posterior sampler evaluation
parts:
Maybe you do not need to involve all predictor in the model, but it
depends on where you want to predict. Yes, if you have other random
effects in the model you have to sample those. You can try on a
smaller example where you can compare with the NA-fillin in INLA.

In the case of SPDE models, there should be some smart functions doing
this, that is used to create the projection matrix...

H
